title: A sunset adventure with a lizard
summary: Two scene pictures animated into one story, with the same characters in every scene.

scenes.prompt:
3D Pixar-style cartoon animation, bright friendly colors, expressive characters. Maintain the exact art style, characters, lighting and layout of the starting frame.

Animate this image for 5 seconds. Vertical 9:16 cinematic 3D animation.

Preserve Dad, Chindu, Kiki, the lizard, hawk and environment exactly as shown.

The detached tail wriggles continuously on the ground.

The hawk stays beside the detached tail and remains completely distracted by it. The hawk looks down, follows the tail movement and tries to grab it.

IMPORTANT: the hawk NEVER flies away and NEVER follows the real lizard.

At the same time, the real tailless lizard runs farther away toward the rocks in the background and reaches safety.

Dad points toward the action and says:

“Some lizards drop their tails to distract predators… and ESCAPE!”

Time Dad's word “ESCAPE!” exactly when the real lizard disappears safely behind the rocks.

Chindu and Kiki watch silently in amazement.

Camera slowly cranes upward and backward, keeping the moving tail, distracted hawk and escaping lizard visible together.

SFX: tail scraping sand, hawk wing movement, desert wind, lizard footsteps.

Music: cinematic discovery music rising toward “ESCAPE!”

Warm golden desert sunlight, airborne dust, natural cinematic motion.

Only Dad speaks.
No narrator.
No female adult voice.
No other voices.
No captions.
No subtitles.
No text.
No blood.
No wounds.
No diagrams.
No arrows.

The hawk MUST remain with the detached tail until the final frame.

Narration voice: a warm, sunny female narrator.

Playful, upbeat background music.

No text overlays, no logos, no watermarks.

Preserve Dad, Chindu, Kiki, the lizard and sunset environment exactly as shown.

This scene takes place much later.

The lizard already has its replacement tail.

DO NOT grow or transform the tail during the video.

Start with the lizard standing proudly on the rock.

Camera slowly moves around the lizard to clearly reveal its replacement tail. The replacement tail remains thicker, smoother and less patterned than the original.

Chindu notices the tail, points toward it and says excitedly:

“It GREW BACK?!”

Dad smiles and answers:

“Many can—but the new tail isn’t exactly the same.”

Kiki reacts silently with amazement.

Immediately after Dad finishes the word “same,” the lizard suddenly runs quickly forward and passes very close beside the camera.

The camera quickly whip-pans to follow the running lizard.

END THE VIDEO DURING THE FAST CAMERA MOVEMENT.

Do not let the camera stop after the lizard runs.

Do not fade out.

SFX: gentle desert wind, lizard claws on rock, quick footsteps and strong whoosh as the lizard passes camera.

Music: soft wonder music, then a quick energetic rise when the lizard runs.

Only Chindu and Dad speak.

Chindu is the older girl in BLUE star pajamas.
Kiki is the younger girl in PINK pajamas.

Kiki does NOT speak.
